hook_text: Trace South Africa's main roads and railways on a map and you will see a wheel. What is at the centre?
clip_script: Gauteng. Gold made it the economic heart of southern Africa, but it is six hundred kilometres from the sea. So every road, railway and pipeline seems to run to it. The N3 climbs from Durban over Van Reenen's Pass: the busiest truck route in the country. The N1 runs from Cape Town to Beitbridge. The N4 heads east to Maputo. Coal trains roll to Richards Bay; iron ore trains to Saldanha Bay. O. R. Tambo is the busiest airport. Eight commercial ports ring the coast, with Durban the busiest of all. And beyond the borders, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Zambia and Lesotho use the same spokes to reach the sea.
visual_style: A whiteboard map of South Africa with Gauteng as a hub, red road spokes and black railway spokes to eight port icons, and arrows continuing across borders.
pacing: Builds the network spoke by spoke.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master transport map questions.
